overall: The AG resolved the complaint by informal action and found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via a July 27, 2023 email; no violation on the chair's separate contact with the accounting firm, and the June 12 email was not investigated.

allegations.summary: Former chair allegedly negotiated the town accountant's resignation and retained an outside accounting firm outside posted meetings, including by a July 2023 email to members.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledges, and we find, that the Board, through Chair D’Amico, violated the Open Meeting Law when she communicated with the other members of the Board outside of a posted meeting, via email on July 27, 2023.

allegations.summary: A June 12, 2023 email, raised in the review request, was alleged to show further out-of-meeting deliberation by the board.
allegations.key_passage: as the June 12 email was not referenced in the original complaint and the Board has acknowledged that it violated the Open Meeting Law in deliberating outside a public meeting, we have not investigated the allegation of a violation on June 12, 2023.

allegations.summary: The former chair allegedly conferred independently with the accounting firm, which was alleged to be an improper out-of-meeting communication.
allegations.key_passage: we do not find a violation, as the communication did not involve a quorum of the Board and therefore did not constitute deliberation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
